avatar.name: G$LIDE Esiah avatar
avatar.canonical_direction: A stylized human portrait with realistic adult human facial proportions and anatomy, rendered as an intentionally unreal layered paper-cut/ink illustration in the G$LIDE palette. The unreal quality comes from paper texture, cut-paper edges, ink/sketch detail, graphic lighting and navy/gold/electric-blue color treatment — not from cartoon anatomy.
required_traits: normal human mouth and jaw proportions
recognizable consistent facial geometry across productions
deep navy, G$LIDE gold and electric-blue treatment
avatar.thumbnail_rule: Every production thumbnail must use the canonical avatar reference image when a human host/avatar is shown. Preserve the reference facial identity and realistic human proportions even under a strong reaction. Use pose, lighting, paper layers and composition for drama instead of changing the person or distorting the face.
avatar.in_video_rule: Any explicit G$LIDE/Esiah avatar appearance inside the video must use the same canonical reference image as thumbnails. Do not switch identity, ethnicity, facial geometry or avatar style between scenes or episodes.
avatar.non_avatar_rule: A normal topic/support visual must not invent a host, presenter or substitute avatar. If a person is not explicitly required by the scene request, use the subject, mechanism, object, environment or diagram instead.

image_generation_rule: If any generated image contains the G$LIDE avatar or a representation of Esiah, the canonical reference image and avatar policy are mandatory. If the image does not contain the avatar, retain the G$LIDE palette and premium paper-cut/technical-explainer visual language without forcing a person into the scene.
qa_rule: A generated avatar that is a different person, changes facial identity, or reads primarily as a cartoon/toon/animated-film character is a brand failure and must not pass release QA.
